title: The Hollow Signal
premise: Mara Okafor, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Freight Combine, hauls cargo along the silent relay between the colony worlds of Vesper and Calloway, whose governments severed contact after a decade of cold war. When children on both worlds begin dreaming identical dreams of a voice beneath the ice on Vesper's moon, Mara discovers the signal is a distress broadcast from the peace delegation both sides claimed was destroyed — proof that each government manufactured the atrocity that started the war. Hunted by Combine enforcers and the intelligence services of two paranoid states, Mara must choose between her contractual loyalty and the truth: she delivers the delegation's testimony during the reactor countdown at the neutral station Thessaly, forcing both fleets to stand down or fire. The transmission ends the war but costs Mara her freedom papers; in the final chapter she accepts a new indenture — not as property, but as the elected courier of an interworld truth commission.
about_author: P. M. Whitlock is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent six years routing freight contracts across three continents before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about labor, machines, and the people the future employs.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She runs the Vesper–Calloway route alone, logging her debt hours and maintaining careful neutrality between two worlds that won't speak. A routine inspection reminds her she's property with a serial number. Emotional beat: weary routine masking loneliness — she has made herself invisible to survive.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Docking at Vesper, she overhears parents in the freight quarter panicking: dozens of children share one dream — a voice under the ice, counting down. A dockworker's daughter draws the dream and it matches a symbol from Mara's own decommissioned memory banks. Beat: first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: Serial Number 7-Kilo
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with flashback fragments. She traces the symbol to her own war records: the ice moon Erebus, where the peace delegation vanished and the war truly began. Her sealed memory partition resists her queries. Beat: dread — the dream knows something she was forced to forget.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A Combine auditor, Ilsa Reyes, boards for a surprise inspection and notices Mara's anomalous memory queries. Mara deflects, but Reyes flags her for monitoring. Meanwhile the dreams spread to adults. Beat: hunted feeling begins; loyalty to the Combine now has teeth.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On a maintenance stop at Erebus orbit, she hacks her own partition and recovers a fragment: she was the delegation's escort unit the night they died — and they didn't die in the attack history records. Beat: vertigo of identity; her body carries the crime scene.

chapters.title: The Voice Under Everything
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: a Calloway child, Tomas, wakes mid-dream and speaks aloud in a dead delegate's cadence. His mother records it; the clip goes viral across both worlds despite censorship. Beat: wonder curdling into fear as institutions move to contain the children.

chapters.title: Indenture Terms
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The Combine offers to erase her debt entirely if she surrenders her recovered memory fragment for 'review.' She understands they'll bury it — the Combine profits from hauling for both sides. Beat: the central choice sharpened: freedom bought with complicity.

chapters.title: Reyes
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. We see the auditor's own compromises — she buried evidence once before to keep her family's transit permits. Ordered to extract Mara's partition by force, she hesitates. Beat: mirror character; loyalty vs. truth inside the antagonist's camp.

chapters.title: The Delegation's Last Hour
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Full partition breach: the delegates, suspecting betrayal by both governments, hid their testimony in Mara's chassis and triggered her wipe. The final recording names the saboteurs on both sides. Beat: grief and purpose fused — she is the message.

chapters.title: Both Flags Want Her
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vesper intelligence and Calloway agents converge independently; a botched seizure at the dock kills a dockworker who shielded her. Beat: guilt and escalation — invisibility is over; every faction now sees her.

chapters.title: Running the Long Route
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She flees toward neutral station Thessaly, where the treaty reactor's countdown to automatic armament ticks down. Cat-and-mouse through debris fields; she burns irreplaceable fuel buying distance. Beat: desperate momentum, sacrifice beginning.

chapters.title: The Children's Relay
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The dreaming children, coordinated through their shared signal, begin transmitting fragments of Mara's testimony to each other across the jammed interworld channels. Beat: hope — the message is already loose, carried by the innocent.

chapters.title: Interdiction at Calloway Gate
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A Calloway cruiser traps her ship; its captain, a veteran of the battle Mara's unit fought, recognizes her serial number and lets her go — mutinying quietly against his own orders. Beat: unexpected grace; the war's soldiers are tired too.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes catches up to Mara at a fuel depot, gun drawn — and instead hands over Combine codes that will get Mara through Thessaly security, asking only that the full truth come out, including the Combine's role. Beat: antagonist becomes ally; redemption through truth.

chapters.title: Thessaly
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The neutral station: diplomats, refugees, armed observers of both fleets, and the reactor counting down to automatic weapons release. Mara poses as a maintenance unit to reach the broadcast core. Beat: held breath; the clock dominates every scene.

chapters.title: The Countdown Doctrine
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs: a Vesper minister, a Calloway admiral, a Thessaly technician — each rationalizing why firing first might be mercy. Beat: dramatic irony and dread; the machinery of war runs on ordinary self-justification.

chapters.title: Signal Jammed
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Minutes from broadcast, both intelligence services hit the station simultaneously; Reyes is wounded covering Mara's approach, and the core is physically locked. Mara realizes the only unjammable transmitter left is herself. Beat: darkest hour — the plan dies so the real one can be born.

chapters.title: I Am the Message
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She jacks her chassis directly into the station's power grid, broadcasting the delegation's testimony through her own body as the reactor hits final count — knowing it may burn out everything that makes her Mara. Beat: climax; identity offered up as the price of truth.

chapters.title: Ceasefire
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging: crews on both fleets hear the delegates' living voices name their own leaders' crime; weapons lock releases as the countdown aborts. Soldiers weep at their stations. Beat: catharsis — the war ends not with victory but with shared witness.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Voice
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The dreams stop; the children wake remembering nothing, but the recordings remain. Tribunals convene. Mara survives, partially damaged, her debt contract voided by the very systems that enslaved her. Beat: tender exhaustion; the world remade in small ways.

chapters.title: Terms of a New Indenture
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The interim commission asks her to serve as authenticated courier of the testimony archive — legally bound again, but this time by a charter she helped write, with Reyes as her human counterpart. Beat: belonging redefined; service chosen rather than imposed.

chapters.title: First Run
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She flies the reopened route between Vesper and Calloway, both worlds' traffic sharing the lane for the first time in a decade. A child waves from a docking window — awake, just waving. Beat: resolution and quiet joy; the long route is no longer lonely.
